title: Probe-driven tenant throttle and eviction ranking for spillover control
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When tenant traffic spikes or misbehaving workloads run (e.g., long-context generation loops, unexpected batch sizes), capacity spillover causes latent degradation for neighboring tenants on shared dedicated pools. Current throttles are static and eviction heuristics are coarse, leading to noisy neighbor incidents and emergency manual interventions.

Goal: Implement a probe-driven tenant throttle and eviction-ranking subsystem that (1) quickly identifies aggressive tenants via lightweight probes and runtime signals, (2) applies graduated soft throttles and credit damping to bound burst impact, and (3) computes an eviction score ranking for graceful spillover enforcement. The system must respect reserved throughput contracts and prefer non-destructive mitigations first.

Success criteria: reduction in P95 tail latency incidents caused by noisy neighbors by >=60% on dedicated pools; fewer manual escalations; predictable tenant degradation paths documented in runbooks. Metrics: tenant P99/P95 latency, preemption events, eviction counts, ticket volume, customer SLA violations.

Design summary: introduce a Probe Agent that continuously samples short synthetic and passive probes for tenant lanes (cost-light token-limited requests) to detect aggressors without impacting real traffic. Combine probe signals with runtime telemetry (queue lengths, per-tenant GPU memory pressure, KV cache hit/miss rates, batch size spikes) into a sliding-window behavioral profile. Compute a multi-factor eviction_score = f(throughput_violation, sustained_queue_growth, memory_pressure, probe_failure_rate, contract_priority, recent_throttle_effectiveness). Eviction_score drives a three-tier mitigation policy: soft dampen (batch caps + rate limit), credit drain (consume burst credits), and targeted preemptive eviction (reclaim slot with graceful draining). All actions emit audit events and rollback hooks.

Compatibility: Works for Dedicated capacity pools and as a fallback for Private deployments with telemetry adapter. Integrates with existing quota/lease service and autoscaler.

Risks and trade-offs: probes add minimal overhead but must be tuned to avoid false positives; incorrect weighting can penalize legitimate high-throughput tenants. Must ensure contract enforcement for reserved customers and provide human-in-loop overrides via Console.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Probe+Driven+Throttles ; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/shipyard/pull/1827 ; dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/eviction/tenant-spillover.

Next steps: finalize scoring weights, land probe agent and sliding window store, add audit + runbook, run chaos tests on staging fleet, gradual canary rollout to low-risk pools.
